newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down after late profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down after late profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mostly lower Friday after a mixed session, hit by a late wave of profit taking despite firmer physical prices from the Arctic cold, industry sources said.
February closed down 16.5 cents at $3.316 per million British thermal units after hitting $3.63 on ACCESS. March settled 23.7 cents lower at $2.849. Most others also were off.

"I think we saw some profit taking today, but sentiment seems to be changing - there's excess hydro, storage is growing and the cold really isn't going to hit the East that much," said one Midwest trader.

While traders said forecasts for below-normal temperatures in the U.S. next week could underpin cash and futures near-term, many expected the first signs of more moderate weather to tank the market, particularly with the storage surplus to last year likely to grow further in coming weeks.

Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with February support still in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.25 and resistance in the $3.80-3.84 area and then at $3.96. The contract high is $4.02.

In the cash, most Gulf prices were up about 30 cents to the $3.85-3.90 range. Midcontinent prices gained about a $1 to the high-$4 area. At the Chicago city-gate, cash prices ranged from a high of $6.50 to a low of $4.50, while New York city-gate values were talked around $4.50.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip slid 6.7 cents to $2.405. NYMEX said an estimated 48,204 Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 40,875.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Friday.

On the KCBT, February closed down 18.9 cents at $3.131, while deferred months finished three to 23 cents lower. The East/West spread widened by 2.4 cents to 18.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 200 contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 364.
